hypothesis: Without retuning, AuroraPIC using the previously qualified eduPIC 1.0 Phelps-based argon package predicts the ETHZ five-pressure consensus drift velocity at 10, 20, and 30 Td within 10% plus two combined simulation/reference standard uncertainties at every field.
prior_information: The collision package previously passed independent-seed comparisons to historical Dutton mobility at 52.8-99.7 Td. A prior unscored 20 Td numerical run informed the long burn and measurement horizon but was not compared with ETHZ. The ETHZ pressure-series values and aggregation rule were inspected before execution, so this is a prospective pass/fail test of a fixed model, not a blind reference acquisition.

reference_contract.source: Haefliger and Franck 2018 ETHZ pulsed-Townsend argon mobility data distributed through the ETHZ LXCat database
reference_contract.interpolation: linear in mobility-times-density between the two bracketing observations in each pressure series; no extrapolation
reference_contract.aggregation: unweighted arithmetic mean across all five pressure series
reference_contract.reference_standard_uncertainty: sample standard deviation across the five interpolated pressure-series drift velocities, not the smaller standard error of their mean
reference_contract.coefficient_compatibility: ETHZ measures temporal swarm transit drift; at 10-30 Td the selected argon model has no nonconservative collisions, so bulk and flux drift coincide

classification: A complete pass extends the independently replicated historical transport result to a modern, explicitly pressure-resolved experiment and to the lower 10-30 Td range. A failure with passing stationarity is evidence against the selected collision package at the failed field; a failure of stationarity remains numerically inconclusive and requires a predeclared extension rather than tolerance changes.
claim_boundary: The experimental paper reports a temperature-controlled laboratory and uses measured temperature to derive number density, while the LXCat rows do not carry pointwise temperature or uncertainty. Cross-pressure sample scatter is therefore used conservatively. This homogeneous fixed-population comparison does not validate self-consistent fields, ions, boundaries, imported geometry, chemistry, or device observables. Phelps-based cross sections may themselves contain swarm constraints, and local LXCat/GPL-derived tables are not redistributed.
